sections.title: Definition & Clinical Overview
sections.content: Posner-Schlossman Syndrome (PSS) is a rare inflammatory glaucoma characterized by acute, recurrent bouts of significantly elevated Intraocular Pressure (IOP), often reaching 40-60 mmHg. Despite the high pressure, symptoms are surprisingly mild, and the anterior chamber reaction is minimal, often self-limiting but potentially damaging to the optic nerve over time.

branches: Viral Trigger: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is the primary suspect; HSV/VZV also implicated.
Trabeculitis: Inflammation of the trabecular meshwork reduces aqueous outflow.
Genetic Factor: Strong association with HLA-B54 (especially in Asian populations).
Autonomic Dysfunction: Possible vascular or sympathetic dysregulation component.

sections.title: Classic Clinical Presentation
content: Sudden onset of mild ocular discomfort or dull ache.
Slightly blurred vision or 'halos' around lights (due to corneal edema).
Eye is usually WHITE and quiet (unlike acute angle-closure).
Recurrent history: Patients often recognize the 'feeling' of an attack.
Mydriasis: The pupil of the affected eye may be slightly larger than the fellow eye.

sections.title: Slit-Lamp Examination Findings
content: Corneal Edema: Fine microcystic edema if IOP is high.
Keratic Precipitates (KPs): Few, discrete, round, white, non-granulomatous KPs (central or inferior).
AC Reaction: Trace to 1+ cells/flare (disproportionately mild for the IOP level).
Gonioscopy: Open angles, no peripheral anterior synechiae (PAS), no neovascularization.
Optic Nerve: Often normal initially, but chronic recurrence leads to glaucomatous cupping.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup & Investigations
content: 1. Goldmann Applanation Tonometry: Confirm IOP elevation.
2. Gonioscopy: Crucial to rule out angle closure.
3. Aqueous Tap (PCR): Test for CMV, HSV, and VZV DNA if recurrence is frequent.
4. Corneal Endothelial Cell Count: Monitor for CMV-induced loss.
5. OCT RNFL & Visual Fields: Baseline and serial monitoring for glaucoma progression.

sections.title: The CMV Connection & Antivirals
content: Topical Ganciclovir 0.15% (Zirgan): Used 4-6 times daily if PCR is CMV positive.
Oral Valganciclovir (Valcyte): Induction dose 900mg BID for 3 weeks, then maintenance 450-900mg QD.
Benefit: Reduces frequency of recurrences and stabilizes IOP.
Caution: Monitor CBC/CMP for systemic side effects (bone marrow suppression).

sections.title: CRITICAL: Prostaglandin Warning
content: Avoid Prostaglandin Analogs (PGAs) during the acute phase.
PGAs can exacerbate intraocular inflammation.
Risk of Cystoid Macular Edema (CME) in an inflammatory state.
Miotics (Pilocarpine) are contraindicated; they may increase inflammation and cause synechiae.

sections.title: Surgical Intervention
sections.content: Surgery is rarely needed for the acute attack. However, if medical therapy fails to prevent progressive glaucomatous damage due to frequent recurrences, a Trabeculectomy or Glaucoma Drainage Device (GDD) may be indicated. Results are generally good, but steroids must be managed carefully.

content.explanation: Sudden High Pressure (40s), Small KPs (Few/Non-granulomatous), Self-limiting (usually resolves in days to weeks).

sections.title: Clinical Pearls & BCSC High Yields
content: Always perform gonioscopy: Unilateral high pressure in a young male is AAC until proven otherwise.
Look for 'Sentinel KPs': Sometimes only 1 or 2 are present.
IOP during episodes is often 40-50, but the optic nerve can look perfectly healthy initially.
Treatment is aimed at lowering IOP first, then controlling the minimal inflammation.
Recent studies suggest checking for CMV in all recurrent or refractory cases.

sections.title: Recent Landmark Insights
sections.content: Contemporary research emphasizes that PSS may not be as 'benign' as once thought. Studies from Singapore and Japan have shown that up to 25% of patients eventually require glaucoma surgery. The role of CMV is now widely accepted, leading to a shift toward using Valganciclovir for recurrent cases to prevent long-term trabecular meshwork scarring.
